what: Is AkashML's 'fp4' Gemma-4-26B-A4B unusually lossy for 4-bit? All five sets of replies re-scored on one referee: Gemma-4-26B-A4B Q8_0 (ggml-org GGUF), lv-engine on llama.cpp 11924d4c1 CUDA, one rented RTX PRO 6000 (Spain). AkashML's, the BF16 honest reference's and the Q4_0 substitute's replies are the ones collected 2026-10-30 (same 48 prompts, greedy, 256 tokens); NVIDIA's official NVFP4 checkpoint (nvidia/Gemma-4-26B-A4B-NVFP4) was served with vLLM 0.32 on the same GPU type as the BF16 reference and collected through the same request path (collect_local_api.py); a Q4_K_M GGUF (lmstudio-community) was generated with lv-engine like the Q4_0 substitute.

greedy_text_overlap_with_bf16.note: AkashML matches no reference word for word (0/48 vs NVFP4); Gemma's replies diverge early under any 4-bit quantization, so this fingerprint is inconclusive

verdict: AkashML's endpoint is labelled fp4, so a loss is disclosed, but it is about 3.3x further from the released model than NVIDIA's own FP4 checkpoint (confidence intervals far apart), further than a Q4_K_M GGUF, and at least as far as the crudest 4-bit format (Q4_0). Whatever it runs is not the standard NVFP4 release served the usual way: possibly a different 4-bit quantization, an additionally compressed KV cache, or other serving changes; replies alone cannot say which. One model, replies from 2026-10-30.
